purpose: Adds three delay JS loading strategies (Interaction, Idle via requestIdleCallback, Viewport via IntersectionObserver) with priority-ordered script loading to improve INP and TBT scores.
riskRationale: Well-structured feature with thorough PHP sanitization and React UI test coverage, but has critical issues: unhandled promise rejections in idle script loading, empty-string entries in strategy lists that match all scripts via strpos('', $handle), and viewport scripts bypassing the priority system entirely.
breakingChanges: New delay strategy/priority data attributes on script tags may affect custom parsers or inline script handlers
Frontend lazy loader now loads scripts by priority order instead of DOM order
New settings keys added to wppo_settings option; old plugin versions will ignore them

text: The PR adds meaningful performance improvements with three delay strategies and priority-ordered script loading. The architecture is clean with good PHP/JS separation, thorough sanitization, and decent UI test coverage. However, the frontend JS engine has critical error-handling gaps: unhandled promise rejections in idle script loading, an empty-string matching vulnerability in PHP strategy resolution, and viewport scripts bypassing the priority system. These must be fixed before merging.

reasoning: Three critical issues block merge: (1) empty-string entries in idle/viewport lists cause strpos('', $handle) to match every script (class-html.php:118); (2) unhandled promise rejections in loadIdleScripts (lazyload.js:218); (3) viewport scripts load individually bypassing the priority system (lazyload.js:253). All are straightforward fixes with clear suggestion code.

message: loadScriptsByPriority provides clean priority-based grouping (high→normal→low) with sequential loading that preserves ordering within each group. Unknown priorities gracefully default to 'normal'.

Properties for delay strategies and priorities are cached in the constructor with clear single-responsibility design — process_urls() handles line-to-array conversion, and the priority map uses explicit valid-value whitelisting via in_array().

Sanitization of delay strategy settings is thorough: absint() for timeout, sanitize_text_field() for list entries, in_array() validation against allowed strategy values, and robust priority parsing via explode(':', ..., 2).
Strategy and priority data attributes are only emitted when they differ from the default ('interaction' / 'normal'), keeping HTML output lean and avoiding unnecessary attribute noise.
Interaction event listeners are only registered when hasInteractionScripts() returns true, avoiding unnecessary event pollution on pages that use only idle/viewport strategies.

Empty-string entries in delay_js_idle_list and delay_js_viewport_list are not filtered after process_urls(). strpos($search_in, '') returns 0 (truthy), causing get_delay_strategy_for_inline() to classify ALL scripts as 'idle' or 'viewport' when a blank line is present in the textarea. The existing exclude_delay_js code at line 115 correctly uses array_filter(..., 'strlen') but the new code omits this guard.
suggestion: Apply the same strlen array filter to delay_js_idle_list and delay_js_viewport_list after process_urls(), matching the pattern used for exclude_delay_js.
suggestionCode:
$this->delay_js_idle_list     = array_values( array_filter( (array) Util::process_urls( $this->options['file_optimisation']['delayJSIdleList'] ?? array() ), 'strlen' ) );
$this->delay_js_viewport_list = array_values( array_filter( (array) Util::process_urls( $this->options['file_optimisation']['delayJSViewportList'] ?? array() ), 'strlen' ) );

message: loadIdleScripts calls async loadScriptsByPriority without await or .catch(), creating an unhandled promise rejection when any individual loadScript() fails (e.g., 404 or network error). loadScript() rejects via replacement.onerror at line 83. The enclosing requestIdleCallback/setTimeout provides no error-containment boundary, so errors are silently swallowed.
suggestion: Await loadScriptsByPriority inside a try/catch block to properly handle and log errors.

message: observeViewportScripts calls loadScript() individually per-script as each enters the viewport, bypassing the priority system entirely. A low-priority script that scrolls into view loads before high-priority scripts still off-screen, defeating data-wppo-delay-priority. The loadScript() calls also have no .catch(), creating unhandled promise rejections on failure.
suggestion: When viewport scripts enter the viewport, batch-load them via loadScriptsByPriority with explicit error handling instead of loading individually.

message: Bidirectional substring matching (strpos($handle, $pattern) || strpos($pattern, $handle)) can produce false-positive strategy matches. For example, pattern 'jquery-ui' matches handle 'jquery' via strpos('jquery-ui', 'jquery') !== false. This makes matching unpredictable for users. The inline-script variant in class-html.php:468 only checks strpos($search_in, $pattern) (single direction), creating an inconsistency between external and inline script behavior.
suggestion: Use consistent single-direction matching (strpos($handle, $pattern)) in both class-main.php and class-html.php. Remove the bidirectional check so substring matching is predictable and consistent across both code paths.

message: loadScriptsByPriority uses sequential await loadScript(script) within each priority group. If one external script fails (404 or network error), the rejected promise propagates, stopping ALL remaining scripts in that group and all lower-priority groups. The caller catches the error but does not continue processing remaining queued scripts.
suggestion: Use Promise.allSettled() within each priority group to prevent a single failure from blocking subsequent scripts while maintaining priority ordering across groups.

message: The setTimeout fallback for browsers without requestIdleCallback uses delayConfig.idleTimeout as the delay argument, but requestIdleCallback's timeout parameter means the callback is triggered within that deadline (max wait), not after that minimum delay. Using idleTimeout directly in setTimeout makes scripts wait much longer than intended when requestIdleCallback is unavailable.
suggestion: Use a shorter explicit delay (e.g., Math.min(2000, idleTimeout)) for the setTimeout fallback instead of reusing idleTimeout directly, since setTimeout's delay is a minimum wait while requestIdleCallback's timeout is a deadline.

message: The condition !hasInteractionScripts() at line 329 is guaranteed to be true because the enclosing else block is only reached when hasInteractionScripts() is false (the if at line 307 requires it truthy). This makes the entire else-if block dead code — the loadScripts() call on line 334 can never execute since PHP only adds data-wppo-delay-strategy for non-interaction strategies.
suggestion: Remove the redundant !hasInteractionScripts() check and simplify to a single guard condition, or replace with a warning log if the unexpected state is detected.

message: delayJSList is created as a copy of options.excludeDelayJS, then mapped back to excludeDelayJS in handleSubmit. This creates a redundant parallel state variable that could get out of sync. If options contains a delayJSList key from a future API version, the spread ...options would override the computed default, breaking the round-trip mapping.
suggestion: Remove delayJSList entirely and use excludeDelayJS directly in both default settings initialization and the submit payload.

message: loadScripts() replaces script elements (preventing double-load) but loadIdleScripts queries [data-wppo-delay-strategy="idle"]. If a script has an idle strategy AND is loaded via interaction before idle fires, the DOM query won't find it since the element was replaced. This is correct behavior but undocumented.
suggestion: Add an inline comment explaining that idle/viewport scripts are removed from the DOM after loading via element replacement, preventing double-load on strategy overlap.

message: The submit-payload test uses expect.objectContaining() with 4 fields but does not assert delayJSIdleTimeout even though it is always included in the payload. The test would pass if the timeout field were accidentally omitted.
suggestion: Add delayJSIdleTimeout to the expect.objectContaining() assertion or test with a non-default value to ensure the field is actually submitted.
suggestionCode:
settings: expect.objectContaining( {
	delayJSDefaultStrategy: 'idle',
	delayJSIdleList: 'jquery-core',
	delayJSViewportList: 'analytics',
	delayJSPriority: 'jquery-core:high',
	delayJSIdleTimeout: 3000,
} )

message: hasInteractionScripts() re-queries the DOM with document.querySelectorAll(...) even though delayedScripts (calculated at line 284) already holds the identical NodeList. The function could accept delayedScripts as a parameter to avoid the duplicate querySelectorAll.
suggestion: Pass delayedScripts as a parameter to hasInteractionScripts() to avoid the duplicate DOM query, or inline the check since it is only called once.

message: The new delay JS engine (loadIdleScripts, observeViewportScripts, loadScriptsByPriority, hasInteractionScripts) has zero automated test coverage. Only the React UI component tests were added. The most critical logic — script attribute-based strategy selection, priority ordering, and idle/viewport initialization — is completely untested.
suggestion: Add Jest tests for lazyload.js using jsdom, covering: idle strategy via requestIdleCallback fallback, viewport strategy with IntersectionObserver mock, priority ordering, and interaction strategy fallback behavior.

message: apply_per_page_delay_config() appends handles to delay_js_idle_list and delay_js_viewport_list without deduplication. If per-page config runs multiple times or a handle is already in the global list, the array accumulates duplicates.
suggestion: Use in_array() to check before appending to prevent duplicate entries.
